papers.title: Dissecting the genetic architecture for maize prolificacy by combining QTL mapping and genome-wide association study.
papers.abstract: Maize prolificacy (ears per plant) is a vital domestication trait in maize that profoundly determines grain yield potential. Deciphering its genetic regulatory network is essential for improving yield performance and expanding germplasm diversity. Here, we performed multi-environment phenotypic evaluation on two RIL populations and one association panel. Integrative QTL mapping and GWAS uncovered 13 QTLs and 8 QTNs associated with maize prolificacy. The stable locus qP9-2 harbored two tissue differentiation-associated genes (Zm00001eb395530, Zm00001eb395480), while the significant SNPs within
papers.journal: Molecular breeding : new strategies in plant improvement
papers.summary: This study combined QTL mapping in two recombinant inbred line populations with a genome-wide association study in an association panel to dissect the genetic basis of maize prolificacy (ears per plant), a key domestication trait affecting yield. The authors identified 13 QTLs and 8 quantitative trait nucleotides, with the stable locus qP9-2 containing two candidate genes linked to tissue differentiation. These findings provide candidate loci and genes that could inform marker-assisted improvement of maize yield potential.

papers.title: DNA methylation signatures from tissue and cell-free DNA in alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency mirror clinical pathologies providing a potential non-invasive tool to monitor liver disease progression.
papers.abstract: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (AATD) is a serpinopathy in which mutations in the SERPINA1 gene cause misfolding of alpha-1 antitrypsin (Z-AAT), leading to hepatic protein accumulation, proteotoxic stress, inflammation, fibrosis, and an increased risk of hepatocellular carcinoma. Despite a uniform genetic mutation in most affected individuals, liver disease severity varies, reflecting contributions from environmental exposures and epigenetic heterogeneity (e.g. DNA methylation). As RNA-interference therapy has emerged as a promising treatment, understanding how epigenetic variation relates to
papers.summary: This study examines DNA methylation patterns in both liver tissue and cell-free DNA from patients with alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency, finding that methylation signatures reflect the clinical pathologies associated with the disease, including inflammation and fibrosis. The authors propose that these epigenetic signatures could serve as a non-invasive tool for monitoring liver disease progression in AATD patients.

papers.title: MaxGeomHash bridges MinHash and FracMinHash for scalable similarity estimation using sub-linear k-mer sketching.
papers.abstract: With the surge in sequencing data generated from biological studies, designing scalable computational techniques has become essential. One effective strategy to enable large-scale computation is to extract k-mers from long sequences, and summarize large k-mer sets into random samples (a.k.a. sketches). These sketches enable rapid estimation of similarity metrics such as Jaccard or cosine, and thus facilitate scalable computations. Popular sketching tools in bioinformatics range from the MinHash algorithm to generate fixed-size sketches; to FracMinHash algorithm to retain a fraction of all k-me
papers.summary: MaxGeomHash is a new sketching method that combines ideas from MinHash (fixed-size sketches) and FracMinHash (fraction-based sampling) to estimate k-mer set similarity more efficiently. It uses sub-linear k-mer sketching, meaning sketch size grows slower than the number of k-mers, enabling scalable similarity estimation on large sequencing datasets. The tool bridges the gap between the two dominant sketching paradigms in bioinformatics.

papers.title: Fast genomic read alignment with minibwa.
papers.abstract: BWA-MEM remains a popular short-read mapper especially for the purpose of variant calling. Several groups have accelerated this algorithm as it has been the performance bottleneck of many current workflows. However, constrained by the original design, these drop-in replacements could only achieve limited speedup. Breaking changes to BWA-MEM are required for further improvement.
papers.summary: The authors present minibwa, a re-engineered short-read aligner that departs from the original BWA-MEM design to achieve substantially faster genomic read alignment while retaining compatibility with variant-calling workflows. By making breaking changes to the original algorithm rather than producing a drop-in replacement, they overcome the speedup limits faced by prior accelerations.

papers.title: Genomic and biological characterization of exopolysaccharides produced by Streptococcus thermophilus CCASU-ST-S3 and CCASU-ST-S52, with statistical optimization and preliminary spectroscopic characterization of EPS-STS3.
papers.abstract: Streptococcus thermophilus is a key dairy starter capable of producing exopolysaccharides (EPS) with strain-dependent biosynthetic and biological properties. Two EPS-producing strains, STS3 and STS52, isolated from yogurt, were characterized genomically, and their partially purified EPS preparations underwent preliminary biological evaluation.
papers.summary: This study genomically and biologically characterizes two Streptococcus thermophilus strains isolated from yogurt that produce exopolysaccharides (EPS), and uses statistical optimization plus preliminary spectroscopy to characterize EPS from strain STS3. The work links strain-level genomic features to EPS biosynthetic and biological properties, highlighting strain-dependent variation relevant to dairy starter selection.

papers.title: ABAQS: A comprehensive scoring method for assessing genome annotation quality.
papers.abstract: As genome resources continue to expand, estimating the accuracy and completeness of genome annotations (e.g., gene and protein models) becomes essential to ensure quality of downstream analyses and applications. It becomes critical in comparative genomic analysis to select genomes with comparable qualities of assembly and annotation. Without careful scrutiny, inconsistencies in annotation quality can undermine downstream studies.
papers.summary: ABAQS introduces a comprehensive scoring method for evaluating the quality of genome annotations, addressing the growing need to assess gene and protein model accuracy and completeness as genome resources expand. The approach helps researchers select genomes with comparable annotation quality for comparative genomics, preventing inconsistencies from undermining downstream analyses.

papers.title: Chromatin compartment shifting is recurrent and associated with epigenetic reprogramming in prostate cancer.
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional chromatin organization shapes gene regulation by partitioning the genome into transcriptionally active and inactive compartments, with implications for prostate carcinogenesis. We integrated Hi-C, ATAC-seq, and transcriptomic data from 18 clinical samples representing benign prostatic hyperplasia, primary prostate cancer (PC), and castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC). Using a computational framework accounting for copy number variation and tumor purity, we characterized A/B chromatin compartment organization in aneuploid tumors. We identified recurrent shifts from inac
papers.summary: This study integrated Hi-C, ATAC-seq, and transcriptomic data from 18 clinical prostate samples to map A/B chromatin compartments across benign, primary, and castration-resistant prostate cancer. They found recurrent shifts in chromatin compartmentalization that are associated with epigenetic reprogramming during prostate cancer progression. The work provides a computational framework for analyzing compartment organization in aneuploid tumors while accounting for copy number variation and tumor purity.

papers.title: From Genomes to Function: Bioinformatics and Multi-Omics Approaches to Insect Chemosensory Receptors.
papers.abstract: Insect chemosensory receptors are essential for detecting environmental chemical cues that influence insect survival and behavior. Advances in genome and transcriptome sequencing have expanded the identification of olfactory receptors (ORs), gustatory receptors (GRs), and ionotropic receptors (IRs), while also providing new opportunities to investigate their expression, evolution, and function. Nevertheless, the functions of many identified receptors remain unknown. This review summarizes recent methods and findings in insect chemosensory receptor research, covering receptor identification and
papers.summary: This review surveys how genome and transcriptome sequencing, combined with multi-omics approaches, are being used to identify and characterize insect olfactory, gustatory, and ionotropic receptors. It highlights that while sequencing has greatly expanded the catalog of known chemosensory receptors, the function of many of these receptors remains unknown, and it summarizes current methods for investigating their expression, evolution, and function.

papers.title: hlafactor: a tool for multi-layer functional annotation of HLA variation.
papers.abstract: The human leukocyte antigen (HLA) system is the most polymorphic region of the human genome and a major determinant of immune function and disease susceptibility. Ideally, analyses of HLA variation would capture multiple layers of information, from classical alleles and amino-acid residues to higher-level functional properties such as tapasin dependency, cell-surface expression, and NK cell ligand groups. However, while allele- and amino-acid-level data are now routinely available, the corresponding functional annotations remain scattered across publications and reference datasets, and no exis
papers.summary: hlafactor is a new software tool that consolidates multiple layers of HLA functional annotation—classical alleles, amino-acid residues, and higher-level properties like tapasin dependency, cell-surface expression, and NK cell ligand groups—into a single resource. It addresses the current fragmentation of HLA functional data across publications and reference datasets, enabling integrated multi-layer analysis of this highly polymorphic immune region.

papers.title: DGIdb in 2026: an interoperable resource for the druggable genome.
papers.abstract: The Drug-Gene Interaction Database (DGIdb; https://dgidb.org) is an open-access aggregate knowledgebase that normalizes and centralizes drug-gene interaction and gene annotation data from diverse therapeutic and biomedical sources. Since its previous update, DGIdb has expanded its data content and added new tooling to better support programmatic access and local deployment. This release updates existing sources and incorporates three new sources of interaction data, including annotation data from the Molecular Oncology Almanac, the PRISM Repurposing Dataset, and the Broad Institute Drug Repurp
papers.summary: DGIdb 2026 is an updated open-access knowledgebase that aggregates and normalizes drug-gene interaction data from many sources, now adding three new datasets including the Molecular Oncology Almanac and PRISM Repurposing Dataset. The release also improves programmatic access and local deployment options, making it easier for researchers to integrate druggable-genome information into their own pipelines.

papers.title: Beyond Mutations: A Seven-CpG DNA Methylation Signature for Predicting HRD in MMRd Colorectal Cancer.
papers.abstract: We previously identified a high level of molecular heterogeneity within mismatch repair deficiency (MMRd) colorectal cancer (CRC). Despite MMRd CRC being typically considered suitable for immunotherapy, only less than half of the metastatic CRC (mCRC) patients achieve complete remission. Thus, the search for identifying new therapeutic targets has become extremely urgent. The use of poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitor (PARPi) has revolutionized the treatment of homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) cancer; however, the HRD prevalence in CRC remains unclear. Here, we conducted an integra
papers.summary: This study identifies a seven-CpG DNA methylation signature that can predict homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) in mismatch repair-deficient colorectal cancer, going beyond mutation-based approaches. The authors integrate methylation data to capture HRD status, which could help identify patients who might benefit from PARP inhibitors. This addresses the unmet need for new therapeutic targets in MMRd CRC, where only a minority of metastatic patients respond to immunotherapy.

papers.title: Multi-centre implementation of a low-coverage whole-genome test for detecting homologous recombination deficiency in ovarian cancer.
papers.abstract: Low-coverage whole-genome sequencing offers a scalable approach to homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) testing in ovarian cancer. This multi-centre study describes the real-world implementation of one such assay, SeqOne SomaHRD, across four European laboratories between 9 January 2023 and 1 October 2025. Tumours were classified as HRD-positive if they had a Genomic Instability score (GIS) of ≥0.50 (GIS-high) and/or a pathogenic BRCA1/2 variant. GIS was generated from two bioinformatically derived measures of genomic instability: Large-scale Genomic Alterations (LGA) and Loss of Parental
papers.journal: The Journal of molecular diagnostics : JMD
papers.summary: This multi-centre study reports real-world implementation of a low-coverage whole-genome sequencing assay (SeqOne SomaHRD) for detecting homologous recombination deficiency in ovarian cancer across four European laboratories. Tumours were classified HRD-positive based on a Genomic Instability score threshold and/or pathogenic BRCA1/2 variants, with the score derived from genomic instability measures including large-scale genomic alterations and loss of heterozygosity. The work demonstrates that low-coverage WGS is a scalable, practical approach for HRD testing in routine clinical settings.

papers.title: DeGenRESOLVE: An offline GUI-based automated nanopore sequencing pipeline for viruses with custom rule-based indel and degeneracy resolution.
papers.abstract: Sequencing methods based on Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) have revolutionized the field of viral genomics. However, available analysis tools are often internet-dependent, have complex installation requirements, or lack graphical user interfaces (GUIs), limiting their use in laboratories with restricted internet access or limited bioinformatics expertise. Here we present DeGenRESOLVE, a pipeline designed for amplicon-based ONT resequencing where a reference genome is available. This pipeline does not perform de novo assembly but processes raw base-called ONT viral sequencing data offline i
papers.summary: DeGenRESOLVE is an offline, GUI-based pipeline for analyzing amplicon-based Oxford Nanopore sequencing data from viruses when a reference genome is available. It automates the workflow and includes custom rule-based resolution of indels and degenerate bases, addressing the need for tools usable in labs with limited internet access or bioinformatics expertise.

papers.title: Epigenome-informed prioritization of bivalent chromatin SNPs enhances genomic prediction robustness: a proof-of-concept study in Pacific white shrimp ( Litopenaeus vannamei).
papers.abstract: Genomic selection has become a powerful tool for accelerating genetic improvement in animal breeding, yet its broader application is often limited by high genotyping costs and reduced predictive reliability across populations. Functional genomic annotations offer a promising strategy to prioritize biologically meaningful variants and improve prediction robustness. Here, using Pacific white shrimp ( Litopenaeus vannamei) as a model, we conducted a proof-of-concept study integrating whole-genome resequencing and phenotypic data from 972 individuals. High-resolution epigenomic maps were generated
papers.summary: This proof-of-concept study in Pacific white shrimp integrates whole-genome resequencing, phenotypic data from 972 individuals, and high-resolution epigenomic maps to prioritize SNPs located in bivalent chromatin regions for genomic selection. The authors show that epigenome-informed SNP prioritization can improve the robustness of genomic prediction while potentially reducing genotyping costs. The work demonstrates how functional genomic annotations can enhance animal breeding programs.

papers.title: Bridging BET bromodomain and immune checkpoint inhibitors through generative bioorganic frameworks for next-generation cancer immunotherapy.
papers.abstract: Bromodomain and extraterminal domain (BET) proteins are epigenetic readers that couple chromatin acetylation to oncogenic and immune-regulatory gene transcription, making them attractive targets for combination with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in precision oncology. This review synthesizes current mechanistic, medicinal-chemistry, and translational evidence on BET-ICI combination strategies. We describe how BET blockade reshapes tumor chromatin architecture, suppresses PD-L1 expression, and enhances antigen presentation, thereby increasing tumor susceptibility to immune-mediated attack
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence on combining BET bromodomain inhibitors with immune checkpoint inhibitors for cancer therapy. It describes how BET blockade alters tumor chromatin architecture, suppresses PD-L1 expression, and enhances antigen presentation, making tumors more susceptible to immune attack. The authors also discuss medicinal-chemistry and translational aspects of these combination strategies.

papers.title: ConGEE: A Statistically Based Approach to the Concordant Gene Expression Evaluation Inside Genome Domains.
papers.abstract: Unraveling the interrelation between the domain organization of eukaryotic genomes and global transcriptional output remains a challenging problem in genomics and is actively under study. Assessing whether genes within specific domain structures are transcriptionally co-expressed necessitates the development of robust analytical tools that retain the inherent clustering of genomic features. Therefore, we developed the ConGEE (Concordance of Gene Expression Evaluation) method, which preserves local expression patterns by shifting expression values along the ordered gene list while randomizing t
papers.summary: ConGEE is a new statistical method for testing whether genes within defined genome domains (such as topologically associating domains) show concordant expression. It preserves local expression patterns by shifting expression values along the ordered gene list while randomizing, providing a robust framework for linking domain organization to transcriptional output. The tool addresses the need for analyses that retain the inherent clustering of genomic features.

papers.title: Computational and experimental strategies for functional validation of non-coding variants in pancreatic cancer.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a highly aggressive malignancy characterised by extensive genomic heterogeneity and limited therapeutic options. Although recurrent coding mutations in key driver genes have been well researched, large-scale sequencing studies have identified a broad array of non-coding variants which may contribute to tumorigenesis by interfering with gene regulatory mechanisms. However, understanding the functional significance of these variants remains a major challenge due to their abundance and the complexity of non-coding regulatory structures. This review outli
papers.summary: This review discusses computational and experimental strategies for functionally validating non-coding genetic variants in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). It highlights the challenge posed by the abundance of non-coding variants identified in sequencing studies and the complexity of regulatory mechanisms, and outlines approaches to determine which variants contribute to tumorigenesis.

papers.title: LGALS1-Associated Candidate Myeloid Signature and In Silico Regulatory Analysis in Ulcerative Colitis: A Bioinformatics Study.
papers.abstract: Background: Ulcerative colitis (UC) substantially impairs patients' quality of life and increases the risk of colorectal carcinogenesis. However, its precise molecular pathogenesis remains to be elucidated. Methods: Bioinformatic tools and methods were used to achieve the objectives of this study. We integrated single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), bulk transcriptome, genome-wide association study (GWAS), and single-cell expression quantitative trait locus (sc-eQTL) data to comprehensively identify key molecular determinants underlying UC. scPagwas and Scissor analyses were performed to iden
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell RNA-seq, bulk transcriptome, GWAS, and sc-eQTL data to identify a myeloid cell signature associated with LGALS1 in ulcerative colitis. Using scPagwas and Scissor analyses, the authors pinpoint candidate regulatory genes and cell populations that may contribute to UC pathogenesis. The work is purely computational and proposes hypotheses rather than experimentally validated mechanisms.

papers.title: Genomic Insights and Comparative Analysis of 'Candidatus Phytoplasma australasiaticum' Associated with Tomato Big Bud Disease in Solanum lycopersicum.
papers.abstract: Phytoplasmas are phloem-localized bacteria with highly reduced genomes that infect plants and insects. Tomato big bud (TBB) is an economically important phytoplasma-associated disease, but genomic information on TBB-associated phytoplasmas remains limited.
papers.summary: This study reports genomic insights into 'Candidatus Phytoplasma australasiaticum', the bacterium associated with tomato big bud disease in tomato plants. The authors provide a comparative genomic analysis of this reduced-genome pathogen, expanding the limited genomic resources available for TBB-associated phytoplasmas. The work helps characterize the genetic basis of this economically important plant disease.

papers.title: Dual-Magnification Deep Learning Predicts KRASG12D Status from H&E Images of Pancreatic Cancer: A Multi-Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: Background: KRAS mutations occur in over 90% of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinomas (PDAC), and KRASG12D is the most frequent variant. G12D-selective inhibitors are now in clinical development, but computational pathology has so far predicted mutation status only at the gene level, leaving allele-specific prediction unexplored. Because genomic testing can be time-consuming and costly, a tool that predicts KRASG12D mutation status from routine hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) images could help identify patients for confirmatory molecular testing and potential treatment with KRASG12D inhibitors. Here w
papers.summary: This study develops a dual-magnification deep learning model that predicts KRASG12D allele-specific mutation status directly from routine H&E-stained pancreatic cancer tissue images. Evaluated across multiple cohorts, the approach moves beyond gene-level KRAS prediction to variant-level inference, potentially helping triage patients for confirmatory molecular testing and G12D-selective inhibitor eligibility.

papers.title: Satellite DNAs Reveal Hidden Repetitive Complexity in the Genome of the Spotted-Wing Drosophila, Drosophila suzukii (Diptera: Drosophilidae).
papers.abstract: Satellite DNAs (satDNAs) are highly repetitive sequences that contribute to genome organization, chromosome structure and evolution. Although studies in several Drosophila species have advanced our understanding of satDNA biology, most species remain unexplored, leaving their evolutionary dynamics and origins poorly understood in a broader context. Here, we characterized the satellitome of the spotted-wing drosophila, Drosophila suzukii (Diptera: Drosophilidae), an economically important pest, integrating computational analyses with cytogenetic mapping. Remarkably, the species presented a high
papers.summary: This study characterizes the satellite DNA (satellitome) of Drosophila suzukii, an economically important pest, using computational analysis combined with cytogenetic mapping. The authors report a remarkably high diversity of satellite DNA families in this species, revealing repetitive complexity that was previously hidden. This expands knowledge of satDNA evolution and genome organization in Drosophila.

papers.title: H3K9 demethylase KDM3A potentiates interferon signaling and macrophage-driven inflammation in atherosclerosis.
papers.abstract: Macrophages drive atherosclerosis through inflammatory activation programs shaped by metabolic and epigenetic reprogramming. H3K9 methylation enforces heterochromatin states and represses transcription, whereas removal of this histone modification creates transcriptionally permissive chromatin. Here, we identified KDM3A-mediated H3K9 demethylation to enhance chromatin accessibility at interferon (IFN) signaling loci, thereby promoting IFN production and downstream IFN-dependent transcriptional and chemokine responses. In a mouse model of atherosclerosis, hematopoietic Kdm3a deficiency reduces
papers.summary: This study shows that the histone demethylase KDM3A removes H3K9 methylation at interferon signaling loci in macrophages, opening chromatin and boosting interferon production and downstream inflammatory chemokine responses. In a mouse atherosclerosis model, deleting Kdm3a in blood cells reduced inflammation, identifying KDM3A as an epigenetic driver of macrophage-driven plaque inflammation.

papers.title: Structural and Molecular Dynamics Analysis of Human β-Defensin 1 Variants Reveals Distinct Perturbation Signatures.
papers.abstract: Human β-defensin 1 (hBD-1) is a small, disulfide-constrained antimicrobial peptide produced predominantly in the kidney and urogenital tract, where it contributes to epithelial innate defense. Genetic variation in the gene encoding hBD-1 has been associated with altered expression levels and susceptibility to infections, including infection following solid organ transplantation, yet the molecular consequences of coding substitutions in the active, mature form remain largely undefined. Here, we integrate conventional genomics, protein bioinformatics, structural modeling, and molecular dynamics
papers.summary: This study uses structural modeling and molecular dynamics simulations to analyze how naturally occurring amino acid substitutions in mature human β-defensin 1 affect the peptide's structure and dynamics. The authors identify distinct perturbation signatures for different variants, suggesting that coding variation could alter the peptide's antimicrobial function and help explain associations with infection susceptibility. The work links genomic variants to molecular-level structural consequences for an innate immune peptide.

papers.title: Genome-Guided Discovery of ShK-like Peptides from Sanderia malayensis with Anti-Amyloidogenic and Neuroprotective Activities.
papers.abstract: While jellyfish venom represents a promising bioresource for biotechnological applications, the extraction of adequate venom amounts and the isolation of pure toxins present significant technical bottlenecks. To overcome these difficulties, a pipeline utilizing bioinformatic analyses was established to identify toxin candidates from genomic datasets, subsequently validating their functions from chemical synthesis. Specifically, a high-quality, 144 Mb genome assembly of the jellyfish Sanderia malayensis was constructed using PacBio CLR long reads (38.2 Gb), Illumina short reads (24.5 Gb), and H
papers.summary: The authors assembled a high-quality 144 Mb genome of the jellyfish Sanderia malayensis and used bioinformatic mining to identify ShK-like peptide toxins, which they then produced by chemical synthesis and functionally validated. The synthesized peptides showed anti-amyloidogenic and neuroprotective activities, demonstrating that genome-guided discovery can bypass the technical bottlenecks of venom extraction and toxin isolation.

papers.title: Genome-Wide Identification and Characterization of the Bromodomain Gene Family in Olive (Olea europaea) and Its Association with Salt Stress Responses.
papers.abstract: Bromodomain (BRD) proteins are evolutionarily conserved epigenetic readers that bind acetylated lysine residues on histone tails, linking chromatin remodeling to transcriptional regulation and abiotic stress adaptation. Although salinity is among the most economically damaging abiotic stresses worldwide, the bromodomain-level epigenetic mechanisms underlying salt tolerance in the perennial crop olive (Olea europaea L.) remain unstudied. This study aimed to identify and characterize the complete Olea europaea bromodomain (OeBRD) gene family in olive, resolve its evolutionary relationships with
papers.summary: This study identifies and characterizes the complete bromodomain (BRD) gene family in olive, an economically important perennial crop, and examines how these epigenetic reader genes respond to salt stress. The authors provide a genome-wide inventory of OeBRD genes, analyze their evolutionary relationships, and link family members to salinity adaptation, offering the first bromodomain-level view of salt tolerance mechanisms in olive.

papers.title: Detection of Maximal Exact Matches in Terabases of Genome Assemblies in Compressed Space and Sublinear Time.
papers.abstract: Detection of long exact matches between a pair of genomes has historically been a fundamental operation in genomics. Similarly, detection of long exact matches between all pairs of haplotypes in a large panel of genotyping array data or whole-genome sequencing variant calls is a fundamental operation in population genetics. Thanks to various recent pangenome efforts, for the first time, large panels of high-quality genome assemblies are being constructed. Therefore, we propose the intersection of these two approaches: detection of long exact matches between all pairs of assemblies in panels of
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The paper introduces a new method for finding long exact matches between all pairs of genome assemblies in large panels, using compressed data structures to achieve sublinear time and space efficiency. This enables scalable comparative genomics across terabase-scale pangenome collections, which was previously computationally prohibitive.

papers.title: Disease-modifying therapies in development for post-traumatic epilepsy.
papers.abstract: Post-traumatic epilepsy (PTE) is a chronic neurological disorder that develops following traumatic brain injury (TBI), a condition affecting nearly 69 million people worldwide. PTE accounts for 20% of acquired epilepsies and is characterized by spontaneous recurrent seizures and long-term neurological deficits. Current antiseizure medications primarily suppress early seizures but do not prevent epileptogenesis or improve long-term neurological dysfunction. This review critically evaluates the current landscape of disease-modifying therapies for PTE with an emphasis on pathophysiological basis,
papers.summary: This review evaluates emerging disease-modifying therapies for post-traumatic epilepsy (PTE), a condition affecting 20% of acquired epilepsies that currently lacks treatments to prevent epileptogenesis or long-term neurological deficits. It emphasizes pathophysiological mechanisms underlying PTE and critically assesses therapeutic candidates in development, highlighting the gap between current antiseizure medications that only suppress early seizures and the need for interventions that modify disease progression.

papers.title: Accelerating discovery and integration from RNA to Protein with R2T2P.
papers.abstract: Integrating transcriptomics and proteomics data remains an unmet challenge in the post-genomics era, discouraging researchers from pursuing integrative approaches to molecular biology research. Leveraging the power of translation profiling, we present RNA to Translation to Protein (R2T2P), a computational platform integrating genome-guided transcriptome assembly with identification of translation and proteins, including a tailored differential analysis framework and support for multiple reference transcriptomes. We applied R2T2P to investigate a cellular model of facioscapulohumeral muscular d
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: R2T2P is a computational platform that integrates transcriptomics and proteomics by combining genome-guided transcriptome assembly with translation and protein identification. It includes a tailored differential analysis framework and supports multiple reference transcriptomes, aiming to make integrative RNA-to-protein analysis more accessible. The authors demonstrate its use in a cellular model of facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy.

papers.title: Multi-omics approaches to unravel the biological effects of DNA-binding small molecules.
papers.abstract: DNA-targeting ligands comprise a diverse class of molecules that bind either canonical duplex DNA or non-canonical DNA structures such as G-quadruplexes. The recent shift towards combining distinct omics approaches, including epigenomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics, is significantly expanding the understanding of the biological effects induced by these small molecules, capturing complex cellular perturbations across multiple molecular layers. Here, we report representative examples from recent literature that illustrate how multi-omics approaches have helped to uncover previ
papers.summary: This review highlights how combining multiple omics approaches (epigenomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics) is expanding our understanding of how DNA-binding small molecules—whether targeting canonical duplex DNA or non-canonical structures like G-quadruplexes—perturb cells across multiple molecular layers. The authors present recent literature examples showing that multi-omics can reveal biological effects that single-omics approaches would miss.

papers.title: A multi-scale cell-type resolved map of trans-regulatory architecture in the aging human brain.
papers.abstract: Mapping genetic effects on distal genes and regulatory programs is essential for understanding how genetic variation influences complex diseases; yet trans-QTL discovery remains limited by weak effect sizes, extensive multiple testing and poor reproducibility. Here, we introduce TransMap, a generalizable computational framework that combines multi-scale trans-QTL mapping with multi-phenotype genetic colocalization to improve the discovery and interpretation of distal regulatory variants. Beyond individual trans-eGenes, TransMap constructs local co-regulatory program phenotypes that account for
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: The authors present TransMap, a computational framework that combines multi-scale trans-QTL mapping with multi-phenotype genetic colocalization to improve discovery and interpretation of distal regulatory variants. Applied to the aging human brain, it constructs cell-type-resolved local co-regulatory program phenotypes, addressing the weak effect sizes and poor reproducibility that have limited trans-QTL studies. The result is a multi-scale map of trans-regulatory architecture linking genetic variation to distal gene regulation across brain cell types.

papers.title: Epigenetic profiling of neuroactive curcumin on histone signatures in breast cancer using gen3DNet.
papers.abstract: Aberrant epigenetic alterations are implicated in the transformation of normal cells into cancerous ones. Unlike genetic mutations, these dysregulations can be reversible and are potential targets for anticancer drugs. Curcumin, a natural plant-derived compound, has been shown to have anticancer effects and neuroprotective properties via its influence on epigenetic regulation. However, the precise nature of these epigenetic changes and the mechanisms driving them remain largely unexplored. Moreover, there is strong evidence linking the neuroactive properties of chemotherapy drugs in the treatm
papers.summary: This study uses a computational approach called gen3DNet to profile how curcumin, a plant-derived compound with both anticancer and neuroactive properties, alters histone modification signatures in breast cancer cells. The work aims to map epigenetic changes induced by curcumin, which are potentially reversible and thus attractive drug targets. The abstract is truncated, so specific quantitative findings are not available.

papers.title: Anticancer activity of sodium propionate in hepatocellular carcinoma cells via downregulation of HDAC2 and HDAC6.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is an aggressive malignancy driven by epigenetic dysregulation. This study investigates the anticancer potential of sodium propionate (SP) as an epigenetic modulator targeting histone deacetylases (HDACs) using an integrated in silico and in vitro approach. Bioinformatics analyses were conducted using publicly available HCC transcriptomic datasets from GEO database, disease gene database (GeneCards database), and chemical-gene interaction networks (Comparative Toxicogenomic Database) to identify potential therapeutic targets, HDAC2 and HDAC6 as key therapeutic ta
papers.summary: This study uses bioinformatics analyses of public HCC transcriptomic datasets to identify HDAC2 and HDAC6 as key epigenetic targets, then tests sodium propionate (a short-chain fatty acid) as an inhibitor of these enzymes in HCC cells. The integrated in silico and in vitro approach suggests SP has anticancer activity mediated through HDAC2/HDAC6 downregulation, pointing to a potential epigenetic therapeutic strategy for liver cancer.

papers.title: Systematic In Silico Analysis of a Conserved Tubulin-Folding Chaperone Network in Plasmodium falciparum: Implications for Microtubule Homeostasis and Antimalarial Targeting.
papers.abstract: Microtubules constitute fundamental cytoskeletal polymers that orchestrate cell division, intracellular trafficking, and the maintenance of cellular architecture across eukaryotic lineages. The biogenesis, folding, and steady-state homeostasis of αβ-tubulin heterodimers are tightly regulated by an evolutionarily conserved cohort of dedicated molecular chaperones, designated tubulin-specific chaperones (TBCs; TBCA-TBCE), acting in concert with the small GTPase Arl2. While this intricate assembly pathway has been extensively dissected in mammalian and plant systems, its existence, molecular arch
papers.summary: This paper uses computational (in silico) methods to identify and characterize the conserved tubulin-folding chaperone network—TBCA through TBCE plus the GTPase Arl2—in the malaria parasite Plasmodium falciparum. The authors argue that this pathway likely governs microtubule homeostasis in the parasite and could represent a new set of antimalarial drug targets. The work is purely computational and does not include experimental validation.

papers.title: Co-mutation of KRAS and ARID1A correlates with the MSI/LINE-1 hypermethylation profile in endometrial carcinoma.
papers.abstract: The interaction between oncogenic signalling and epigenetics in endometrioid endometrial carcinoma (EEC) is poorly defined. We investigated the potential association of KRAS-ARID1A co-mutation axis with a distinct hypermethylator phenotype, affecting focal MLH1 promoter methylation and global DNA methylation (LINE-1).
papers.summary: This study examines whether co-occurring KRAS and ARID1A mutations in endometrioid endometrial carcinoma are associated with a distinct DNA hypermethylation phenotype, including focal MLH1 promoter methylation and global LINE-1 methylation. The authors report that KRAS-ARID1A co-mutation correlates with the MSI/LINE-1 hypermethylation profile, suggesting an interaction between oncogenic signaling and epigenetic dysregulation in this cancer.

papers.title: CALB1 expression in meningioma: associations with progression-free survival and chromosome arm 6q loss.
papers.abstract: Molecular profiling has refined risk stratification in meningioma, but the biological relevance of associated transcriptional changes remains incompletely understood. Calbindin D28K (Calb), encoded by CALB1, is a calcium-binding protein with reported anti-apoptotic and cytoprotective functions. Previous unsupervised transcriptomic analysis identified CALB1 upregulation in meningiomas with aggressive cellular features, but its biological and clinical relevance remains unresolved. We analysed Calb immunoreactivity in 231 meningioma tissue microarray (TMA) cores from 147 patients and evaluated CA
papers.summary: This study examined calbindin D28K (CALB1) protein expression in 231 meningioma tissue samples from 147 patients and found associations between CALB1 expression, progression-free survival, and chromosome arm 6q loss. The findings suggest CALB1 may serve as a clinically relevant biomarker linked to aggressive meningioma biology, though the abstract is truncated before full results are reported.

papers.title: MoleMap: fast alignment-free molecule mapping for long-read and linked-read sequencing data.
papers.abstract: With sequencing costs continuing to decline, the computational expenses of read alignment in genome analysis are becoming an increasingly important consideration. When only portions of the genome are of interest - as in most clinical genome analyses - or base-pair precise alignment is not required, performing full read alignment on whole-genome sequencing (WGS) data imposes unnecessary computational costs. Alignment provides the base-by-base precision necessar​y to identify variants relative to a reference sequence. To improve efficiency, sequence reads can first be rapidly mapped to approxima
papers.summary: MoleMap introduces a fast, alignment-free method for mapping long-read and linked-read sequencing data to approximate genomic locations. By avoiding full base-pair alignment, it reduces computational costs when only portions of the genome are of interest or when precise alignment is unnecessary. The tool is designed to improve efficiency in clinical genome analyses and other applications where rapid mapping suffices.

papers.title: gcat, its_a_scam: modular tools for single cell data processing and per-cell quality control.
papers.abstract: The era of designing bioinformatic pipelines using open source tools is giving way to monolithic, and often proprietary, tools designed for end-to-end analysis, especially in the context of single cell data. While these tools are convenient for going from sequencing data to an almost complete data analysis "in a few clicks", they can strongly limit data use beyond standard analyses.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors present gcat and its_a_scam, two modular open-source tools for processing single-cell sequencing data and performing per-cell quality control. These tools aim to counter the trend toward monolithic, often proprietary end-to-end pipelines by giving researchers flexible, composable components that preserve data usability beyond standard workflows.

papers.title: Molecular mechanisms of colorectal cancer: from carcinogenesis and molecular classification to targeted therapy.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a heterogeneous disease that results from the progressive accumulation and interactions at multiple levels of genetic alterations, which lead to the transformation of normal colonic epithelium into malignant colorectal tumors. Understanding the molecular basis of CRC pathogenesis, together with the interactions between genetic alterations, epigenetic modifications, environmental and lifestyle factors, is essential for improving prevention, diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment strategies. This review aims to provide a critical reference point for understanding the temp
papers.summary: This review synthesizes the molecular mechanisms driving colorectal cancer, from the stepwise accumulation of genetic and epigenetic alterations during carcinogenesis to the current molecular classification systems used to subtype tumors. It also covers how these mechanistic insights inform targeted therapy strategies, emphasizing the interplay between genetic changes, epigenetic modifications, and environmental/lifestyle factors in shaping prevention, diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment.

papers.title: Variant Classification of a Non-Protein Coding Gene: ACMG/AMP Specifications for RMRP from the Clinical Genome Resource Severe Combined Immunodeficiency Disease Variant Curation Expert Panel.
papers.abstract: This study, conducted by the Clinical Genome Resource Severe Combined Immunodeficiency Disease Variant Curation Expert Panel (ClinGen SCID-VCEP), aimed to adapt the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics/Association for Molecular Pathology (ACMG/AMP) framework for germline variant interpretation in RMRP . Unlike the protein-coding genes for which the framework was primarily developed, RMRP encodes a non-protein-coding RNA. Biallelic pathogenic variants in RMRP cause cartilage-hair hypoplasia, which can include severe combined immunodeficiency disease and other immune abnormalities.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This work adapts the ACMG/AMP germline variant interpretation framework specifically for RMRP, a non-protein-coding RNA gene where biallelic pathogenic variants cause cartilage-hair hypoplasia and associated immunodeficiency. The ClinGen SCID Variant Curation Expert Panel provides gene-specific specifications that extend the standard framework—designed for protein-coding genes—to a non-coding gene context.

papers.title: Lysine crotonylation acts as an epigenetic switch for glutamate neurotransmission and spatial memory.
papers.abstract: Histone posttranslational modifications, particularly lysine acetylation (Kac), are critical epigenetic regulators of transcriptional programs underlying long-term memory consolidation. Beyond Kac, several other non-acetyl acylations have been identified with the ability to regulate transcription; however, their role in memory consolidation remains unknown. Here, we identify histone lysine crotonylation (Kcr) as a molecular switch for long-term memory and glutamatergic neurotransmission. We find that spatial learning induces distinct spatiotemporal patterns of Kcr across hippocampal subregions
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.summary: This study identifies histone lysine crotonylation (Kcr), a non-acetyl posttranslational modification, as a key epigenetic regulator of long-term memory consolidation. Spatial learning produces distinct spatiotemporal patterns of Kcr across hippocampal subregions, and Kcr appears to act as a molecular switch controlling glutamatergic neurotransmission and spatial memory. The work extends the known epigenetic repertoire beyond histone acetylation in the context of memory formation.

papers.title: Systematic benchmarking of Hi-C-based scaffolding methods in genome assembly.
papers.abstract: High-throughput chromosome conformation capture (Hi-C) technology is crucial for scaffolding, a key step to generate chromosome-level high-quality genome assemblies. However, although several Hi-C-based scaffolding tools have been developed, their utility in genome assembly remains constrained by inconsistent performance, making a systematic benchmarking urgently needed. Here, we present a comprehensive benchmark of five prominent Hi-C scaffolders using simulated contig assemblies considering various factors, including contig lengths, chimeric contig proportions, Hi-C coverage depths, and ploi
papers.summary: This paper systematically benchmarks five Hi-C-based scaffolding tools across simulated contig assemblies, varying contig length, chimeric contig proportion, Hi-C coverage depth, and ploidy. It identifies performance differences and provides guidance on tool selection and parameter choices for chromosome-level genome assembly. The benchmark fills a gap in standardized evaluation of Hi-C scaffolders.

papers.title: XenoMix: estimating mouse content from DNA methylation data of Patient-Derived Xenograft models.
papers.abstract: DNA methylation microarrays enable cost-effective, high-throughput profiling of human and mouse samples and are widely used to study epigenetic alterations in cancer. Patient-Derived Xenograft (PDX) models complement this approach by preserving primary tumor characteristics while enabling in vivo studies of drug response and therapy resistance. However, it remains difficult to quantify mouse DNA contamination in PDX DNA methylation data generated using microarrays. We present XenoMix, a light-weight computational tool for quantifying mouse DNA contamination directly from DNA methylation data i
papers.summary: XenoMix is a lightweight computational tool that estimates the proportion of mouse DNA contamination in Patient-Derived Xenograft (PDX) samples profiled with DNA methylation microarrays. It addresses the common problem of mixed human-mouse signal in PDX methylation data, enabling researchers to quantify and account for mouse content without additional experimental steps.

papers.title: quarTeT after 3 years: toolkit updates and community insights for telomere-to-telomere genome assembly.
papers.abstract: Since its initial release in 2023, quarTeT has become a widely used toolkit for telomere-to-telomere (T2T) genome assembly and characterization. Here, we present a major update that improves all four quarTeT modules, including optional contig filtering in AssemblyMapper, a refactored join algorithm in GapFiller, enhanced telomere detection in TeloExplorer (TE), and support for holocentric chromosomes in CentroMiner (CM). The main program has also been upgraded with user-configurable multithreading, broader version compatibility, and simplified deployment via Bioconda, Docker, and Singularity.
papers.summary: quarTeT, a toolkit for telomere-to-telomere genome assembly and characterization, receives a major update improving all four of its modules: contig filtering in AssemblyMapper, a refactored join algorithm in GapFiller, enhanced telomere detection in TeloExplorer, and holocentric chromosome support in CentroMiner. The main program adds configurable multithreading, broader version compatibility, and simplified deployment via Bioconda, Docker, and Singularity.

papers.title: Unveiling Key Gene Signatures in Pancreatic Cancer: Advanced Computational Insights for Biomarker and Therapeutic Target Discovery.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains the most lethal type of pancreatic cancer, with a dismal 11% 5-year survival rate, owing to its rapid progression and metastasis. Its aggressive nature, coupled with late diagnosis and inadequate therapeutic approaches, necessitates the urgent identification of novel disease-associated genes for more targeted therapy. Using the extensive RNA-seq and microarray data from PDAC patients, this study aimed to computationally screen differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between tumor and non-tumor samples to discover potential biomarkers and therapeuti
papers.summary: This study computationally analyzed RNA-seq and microarray data from pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) patients to identify differentially expressed genes between tumor and non-tumor samples. The goal was to uncover candidate biomarkers and therapeutic targets for this highly lethal cancer, which has limited treatment options and poor survival rates.

papers.title: MLMP: A Methylation-Associated lncRNA-mRNA Prognostic Signature for Endometrial Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Endometrial carcinoma (EC) is one of the most common gynecological malignancies. Aberrant DNA methylation (DNAm) is an important epigenetic alteration involved in cancer progression. Long non-coding RNAs (LncRNAs) play critical roles in gene regulation and pathological processes. However, the biological and prognostic significance of lncRNA-mRNA pairs associated with methylation remains unclear.
papers.summary: The authors construct a prognostic signature for endometrial carcinoma by integrating DNA methylation data with lncRNA-mRNA expression pairs, identifying methylation-associated lncRNA-mRNA modules linked to patient survival. This provides a multi-omic biomarker framework that may improve risk stratification beyond standard clinical variables. The work is a disease-specific extension of established signature-building approaches.

papers.title: Epigenetic Insights in Pediatric Multiple Sclerosis: DNA Methylation Highlights an Involvement of Epstein-Barr Virus Infection and Host Immune Networks.
papers.abstract: Pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis (PedMS) provides a unique opportunity to investigate MS pathogenesis because of the short interval between environmental exposures and disease onset. This study aimed to identify differentially methylated regions (DMRs) that mediate the interplay between environmental triggers and genomic factors in the early stages of the disease.
papers.summary: This study identifies differentially methylated DNA regions in pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis patients, highlighting epigenetic links to Epstein-Barr virus infection and host immune networks. The findings suggest that EBV exposure may interact with host immune gene regulation via DNA methylation in early MS pathogenesis.

papers.title: MethyAnno: An Interpretable Automated Annotation Method Leveraging Multi-Scale Information and Metric Learning Framework for scDNAm Data.
papers.abstract: Single-cell DNA methylation (scDNAm) sequencing provides unique insights into epigenetic heterogeneity and cell-specific regulatory landscapes. However, accurate cell type annotation for scDNAm data remains challenging, as the distinct data distribution of scDNAm hinders the adaptation of annotation methods from other omics, and specialized annotation tools for scDNAm are currently lacking. Here, MethyAnno is proposed as an interpretable deep metric learning framework that leverages multi-scale information for accurate cell type annotation of scDNAm data. Additionally, MethyAnno enables genera
papers.summary: MethyAnno is a new interpretable deep metric learning framework for automatically annotating cell types in single-cell DNA methylation (scDNAm) data, a modality that lacks specialized annotation tools due to its distinct data distribution. It leverages multi-scale information to improve accuracy and interpretability, addressing a key gap in single-cell epigenomics analysis.

papers.title: Assessing the predictive potential of the Holstein bovine sperm methylome for bull fertility using machine learning.
papers.abstract: Bull fertility is a key parameter in the dairy cattle industry, with significant economic implications. DNA methylation is an epigenetic mark essential for fertility, and recent works have highlighted sperm DNA methylation as a promising source of biomarkers for male fertility, but no operational tool has been developed for predicting bull fertility based on DNA methylation. Here, we leveraged existing methylation data to evaluate the potential of DNA methylation for predicting bull fertility with machine learning models.
papers.summary: This study tested whether DNA methylation patterns in Holstein bull sperm can predict bull fertility using machine learning models. Using existing methylation data, the authors evaluated the predictive power of these epigenetic marks as biomarkers for male fertility in dairy cattle. The work represents an initial step toward developing operational tools for fertility prediction based on sperm DNA methylation.

papers.title: Gestational Pyrethroid Exposure and Placental Health in Wistar Rats: Evaluation of Epigenetic, Developmental, and Oxidative Stress Biomarkers.
papers.abstract: Understanding the mechanisms of placental toxicity provides an important research tool that can help to clarify how early-life exposure may influence adverse pregnancy outcomes, foetal health, and long-term disease risk in adulthood. In the present study we estimated the effects of oral gestational exposure to the pyrethroid insecticide α-cypermethrin (α-cyp), a potential endocrine disruptor, in doses of 1, 10, and 19 mg/kg bw/day on different parameters in placentas of Wistar rats (n = 5 per group; 30 animals in total). We evaluated global DNA methylation within the LINE1 repetitive region us
papers.summary: This study examined how oral exposure to the pyrethroid insecticide α-cypermethrin during pregnancy affects placental health in Wistar rats. The authors measured global DNA methylation in the LINE1 repetitive region along with developmental and oxidative stress biomarkers across three dose groups. The work aims to clarify mechanisms by which early-life pesticide exposure may influence placental toxicity and downstream pregnancy and health outcomes.

papers.title: Pathogen surveillance by agnostic high-throughput sequencing in sand flies collected in the country of Georgia.
papers.abstract: Sand flies are known vectors of human pathogens that cause acute febrile illness (AFI). Understanding the pathogen landscape within these insects is crucial for biosurveillance and prevention of infectious diseases in U.S forces deployed to regions where sand flies are present.
papers.summary: This study used agnostic high-throughput sequencing to survey pathogens in sand flies collected in the country of Georgia, aiming to characterize the viral and bacterial landscape carried by these vectors of acute febrile illness. The work supports biosurveillance efforts relevant to military deployments in regions where sand flies are present. It provides a baseline pathogen inventory for an understudied region.

papers.title: Subtractive Genomic Approach for Identification of Pathogen-Specific Essential Genes as Target and Drug Repurposing in Major Foodborne Bacteria.
papers.abstract: Foodborne diseases pose a substantial threat to global public health and economic stability, with bacterial contamination occurring at multiple stages of the food supply chain. The rapid emergence of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) among foodborne pathogens has further complicated the prevention and treatment of these infections, underscoring the urgent need for novel, pathogen-specific therapeutic targets. In this study, a comprehensive subtractive genomics approach was employed to systematically identify bacterial key genes (bKGs) as drug targets and to explore corresponding potential therape
papers.summary: This study applies a subtractive genomics pipeline to identify essential genes unique to major foodborne bacterial pathogens (absent from the human host), nominating them as pathogen-specific drug targets. The authors then perform drug repurposing to find existing compounds that could inhibit these targets, offering a computational route toward new antimicrobials against resistant foodborne infections.

papers.title: In silico analysis toward functional genomic profiling and bioprospecting Serratia rubidaea VITVS26 for its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant potential.
papers.abstract: Proteases from bacteria and their secondary metabolites have bioactivity which can be utilized in therapeutical industries to overcome the negative effects of existing conventional medicines.
papers.summary: This study performs an in silico genomic and functional profiling of the bacterium Serratia rubidaea VITVS26 to identify genes and secondary metabolites with potential anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activity. The authors use computational bioprospecting to predict protease and metabolite functions, highlighting the strain as a candidate source for therapeutic compounds. The work is entirely computational and lacks experimental validation.

papers.title: Identification and structural characterization of MMP1 and MMP9 as potential targets of curcumin and resveratrol in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is a major subtype of lung cancer characterized by substantial molecular heterogeneity and limited therapeutic options. Curcumin and resveratrol are naturally occurring bioactive compounds with reported anticancer activities, but their potential molecular targets and mechanisms in LUAD remain incompletely characterized.
papers.summary: This study uses computational approaches to identify MMP1 and MMP9 as potential molecular targets of the natural compounds curcumin and resveratrol in lung adenocarcinoma, then structurally characterizes the predicted binding interactions. The work suggests a mechanistic rationale for the reported anticancer effects of these polyphenols in LUAD, though the findings are based on in silico docking and network analyses rather than experimental validation.

papers.title: Epigenetic modification of neurotransmitter pathways during fasting: a systematic review.
papers.abstract: Dietary restriction, encompassing intermittent fasting and caloric restriction, represents a prominent non-pharmacological approach to modulating brain aging and neuronal resilience. Emerging evidence links metabolism to long-term neural plasticity through epigenetic mechanisms, yet findings remain fragmented. This review integrates preclinical evidence on how dietary restriction alters brain epigenetic regulation and links these changes to neurocognitive outcomes.
papers.summary: This systematic review synthesizes preclinical evidence showing that dietary restriction (intermittent fasting and caloric restriction) alters brain epigenetic regulation, particularly within neurotransmitter pathways, and links these changes to neurocognitive outcomes. The authors argue that metabolism influences long-term neural plasticity through epigenetic mechanisms, though the existing findings are fragmented across studies.
